# Soniq

> Background jobs for FastAPI and any asyncio app, stored in the PostgreSQL you already have. No Redis, no separate broker. Async-native workers, transactional enqueue (insert the job in the same DB transaction as your business write), built-in dashboard, scheduler, and dead-letter queue.

This file is for AI agents and indexing tools following the [llms.txt convention](https://llmstxt.org). It points to the canonical pages an agent needs to write working Soniq code without browsing the rest of the docs. The full canonical surface is also concatenated into [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) for one-shot context loading.

If you are an agent generating Soniq code, the most common four mistakes are:

1. Calling the decorator without parens (`@soniq.job` instead of `@soniq.job()`). Always use parens.
2. Passing job arguments positionally to `enqueue` (`await soniq.enqueue(send, "a@b.com")`). Job args are keyword-only - use `to="a@b.com"`.
3. Forgetting `await` on `enqueue` from sync code. Wrap in `asyncio.run(...)` for one-shot scripts.
4. Returning a non-JSON-serialisable value from a handler. Soniq stores results as JSONB - anything else is logged as an error and stored as `None`. Return dicts, lists, scalars, or persist large outputs out-of-band and return a reference.

Read [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) at the repo root for a longer agent-targeted brief.

## Start here

- [Quickstart](quickstart.md): five-minute path from `pip install` to first job. Canonical shape of `Soniq(database_url=...)`, `@soniq.job()`, `await soniq.enqueue(...)`, `soniq setup`, `soniq worker myapp.jobs:soniq`.
- [Why Soniq?](why-soniq.md): the case for picking Soniq over Celery/RQ/Arq. Trade-offs and when NOT to use it.
- [Compare tools](compare.md): Soniq next to Celery, RQ, arq, Taskiq and the other Postgres-backed queues, with when to pick each.
- [Benchmarks](benchmarks.md): throughput and latency numbers, the machine, and how to reproduce them.
- [Stability and versioning](stability.md): what stays stable between releases and how breaking changes are announced.
- [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md): the agent-targeted brief - canonical patterns, anti-patterns, and where to look up details.

## Tutorial (read in order; ~30 minutes total)

- [1. Defining jobs](tutorial/01-defining-jobs.md): `@soniq.job()`, decorator kwargs, validation with Pydantic, JobContext.
- [2. Running workers](tutorial/02-running-workers.md): `soniq worker`, concurrency, queues, signal handling.
- [3. Retries](tutorial/03-retries.md): `retries`, `retry_delay`, `retry_backoff`, idempotency.
- [4. Scheduling](tutorial/04-scheduling.md): `@soniq.periodic(cron=...)`, `@soniq.periodic(every=...)`, the scheduler service.
- [5. Queues](tutorial/05-queues.md): queue routing, priority, per-queue workers.
- [6. Transactional enqueue](tutorial/06-transactional-enqueue.md): atomic job + business write via `connection=conn`.

## Reference (look up by name)

- [Python API: Soniq](api/soniq.md): `Soniq(...)` constructor, lifecycle (`ensure_initialized`, `close`), and `soniq.*` services (scheduler, dead_letter, webhooks).
- [Python API: Jobs](api/jobs.md): `@soniq.job()`, `@soniq.periodic()`, `enqueue()`, `schedule()`, `JobContext`, `JobStatus`, the `soniq.schedules` cron DSL.
- [Python API: Worker](api/worker.md): `soniq worker` CLI, `soniq.run_worker()`, env-var configuration, graceful shutdown.
- [Python API: Hooks](api/hooks.md): `@soniq.before_job`, `@soniq.after_job`, `@soniq.on_error` for logging, metrics, tracing.
- [CLI commands](cli/commands.md): `setup`, `worker`, `scheduler`, `dashboard`, `inspect`, `dead-letter`, `status`, `migrate-status`.
- [Dead-letter queue](reference/dead-letter.md): how the DLQ works, how to inspect, replay, and purge.
- [Storage format](reference/storage-format.md): the tables and JSON rules for reading and writing jobs from any language, and the `args_hash` algorithm.
- [Deprecations](deprecations.md): deprecated names, when they go away, and what to use instead.
- [Glossary](reference/glossary.md): one-paragraph definitions for the words the docs use (job, handler, task name, worker, scheduler, queue, heartbeat, DLQ, replay, at-least-once, transactional enqueue, backend).

## Guides (task-shaped, not API-shaped)

- [FastAPI](guides/fastapi.md): the `lifespan()` helper, running the worker in the API process, moving it out later, and moving off `BackgroundTasks`.
- [Transactional enqueue](guides/transactional-enqueue.md): pass a SQLAlchemy `AsyncSession` or `AsyncConnection`, a raw asyncpg connection, or a psycopg 3 connection as `connection=`. Tortoise works through a private attribute.
- [Common patterns](guides/common-patterns.md): idempotency, fan-out, retry policies, deduplication keys.
- [Testing](guides/testing.md): in-memory backend, `run_once=True`, `soniq.testing.drain`, the opt-in pytest plugin.
- [Cross-service jobs](guides/cross-service-jobs.md): enqueue by string name or `TaskRef` when producer and consumer live in different repos.

## Migration

- [Migrating to Soniq](migration/index.md): trade-offs, what's the same on both paths, and how the migrations coexist with your old queue.
- [From Celery](migration/from-celery.md): full concept map (`@app.task` -> `@soniq.job()`, Beat -> the scheduler, result backend -> `soniq_jobs.result`), what Celery has that Soniq does not (chains/chords, pickle, `bind=True`), module-at-a-time sequence.
- [From RQ](migration/from-rq.md): concept map (registries collapse into a four-state `status` column, `Retry(...)` -> `@soniq.job(retries=...)`), six-step mechanical sequence.

## Production

- [Going to production](production/going-to-production.md): the eight things that matter for a healthy deploy.
- [Deployment overview](production/deployment.md): prerequisites, queue routing, performance tuning. Pointers to [systemd](production/deployment-systemd.md), [Docker Compose](production/deployment-docker-compose.md), [Kubernetes](production/deployment-kubernetes.md), and [supervisor](production/deployment-supervisor.md).
- [PostgreSQL tuning](production/postgres.md): connection pool sizing, autovacuum, partitioning.
- [Migrations with Alembic](production/migrations.md): export Soniq's schema SQL with `soniq migrations export` and apply it from your own migration tool.
- [Reliability](production/reliability.md): graceful shutdown, stuck-job recovery, scheduler failover.
